::: {.patient-banner}
## Aphasia Assessment & Clinical Decision-Making

Today's simulation focuses on language assessment, communication strategies, and clinical decision-making for a patient with a history of left hemisphere stroke.

Students will review medical and interdisciplinary documentation, identify communication barriers, determine readiness for language assessment, and administer the Quick Aphasia Battery (QAB). Students will interpret findings in the context of functional communication, patient participation, and discharge planning.
:::

::: {.warning}
## SLP Task

You have received a consult for a language evaluation for Steven "Steve" Thompson, a 94-year-old male admitted following a fall with a history of left hemisphere cerebrovascular accident (CVA).

Review the available clinical information to determine whether Steve is appropriate for language assessment at this time.

If appropriate, administer the Quick Aphasia Battery (QAB), identify receptive and expressive language strengths and difficulties, and develop recommendations to support functional communication.

Throughout the session, consider how Steve's medical history, current presentation, and communication abilities may influence assessment, patient participation, and clinical recommendations.
:::

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this session, students will be able to:

- Identify language impairments commonly associated with left hemisphere stroke.
- Gather relevant information from medical and interdisciplinary documentation.
- Evaluate patient readiness for language assessment based on medical, cognitive, and communication factors.
- Identify and implement supportive communication strategies for individuals with aphasia.
- Demonstrate appropriate administration of the Quick Aphasia Battery (QAB).
- Interpret language assessment findings while recognizing the limitations of standardized assessment.
- Connect language findings to functional communication, patient participation, safety, and discharge planning.
- Communicate findings and recommendations using professional, patient-centered language.

---

## Today's Modules

### 1. Medical Chart Review

Review Steve Thompson's medical history, current hospitalization, neurological history, medications, prior level of function, and reason for SLP consultation.

Identify relevant clinical information and consider how his history of left hemisphere stroke may influence language functioning.

[Begin Chart Review](chart.html)

### 2. Interdisciplinary Documentation

Review documentation from nursing, occupational therapy, physical therapy, and the medical team.

Identify observations related to Steve's communication abilities, participation in care, and functional independence.

Consider how interdisciplinary findings may inform your language assessment plan.

[Review Interdisciplinary Notes](interdisciplinary.html)

### 3. Communication Considerations

Evaluate Steve's current communication abilities and identify strategies to support successful interactions during the assessment.

Discuss how to modify instructions, verify comprehension, support expression, and facilitate patient participation without compromising the purpose of standardized testing.

[Explore Communication Strategies](communication.html)

### 4. Language Assessment & Functional Implications

Administer the Quick Aphasia Battery (QAB) during the simulation, as appropriate.

Interpret findings across receptive and expressive language domains and discuss how identified strengths and difficulties may influence functional communication, participation in medical care, and discharge planning.

Consider whether additional assessment, communication supports, or caregiver education may be warranted.

[Explore Functional Implications](implications.html)
